title: Users can’t resolve internal hostnames
summary: Multiple workstations report intermittent DNS lookup failures for internal domains.

triage.q: What is the best first triage step?
options: Verify scope and impact across users/subnets
Flush DNS cache on all endpoints

diagnosis.q: What evidence most strongly points to the likely cause?
options: Clients can’t ping the DNS server
DNS client timeouts with server reachable
Update DNS forwarder configuration and validate recursion

validations: Check DNS server event logs for new errors

debrief.title: Resolution Summary
debrief.summary: The issue presented as client-side DNS timeouts, but connectivity to the DNS server was healthy. By confirming scope/impact and then validating DNS recursion behavior, we isolated the failure to upstream resolution and corrected the forwarder configuration.
whatGoodLooksLike: Start by confirming impact and narrowing the blast radius (who/where/how many).
Separate connectivity issues from name-resolution logic issues.
Make one controlled change, then re-test from multiple vantage points.
validation: Verify name resolution from multiple subnets and a test host.
Confirm internal records resolve consistently over several attempts.
Review DNS logs to ensure errors stop after the change.
debrief.takeaway: Don’t guess—triage scope first, then validate the resolution path end-to-end.
